newsitem.title: INDIA: Cyclone threatening southeast India intensifies.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone threatening southeast India intensifies.

text.p: A cyclone threatening southeast India, which is still counting its dead from a storm last month, gathered strength and could hit the coast by Tuesday evening, Andhra Pradesh state officials said on Monday.
A relief official in Hyderabad said the storm was building up to become more powerful than the one that left more than 2,000 people either dead or missing in early November.
The Indian meteorological department in New Delhi said the cyclone was 650 kilometres (405 miles) east-southeast of Machilapatnam on the Andhra Pradesh coast at 8.30 a.m. (0330 GMT) on Monday.

It said the storm was likely to intensify further as it moved in a west-northwest direction. Thundershowers and high winds were expected along the coast of Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring Orissa state.

"It (the storm) is moving very slowly," a senior official at the relief control room in Hyderabad told Reuters, adding that it could strike the coast on Tuesday evening based on current speed and direction.
Cyclone warnings have been sounded in low-lying areas, fishermen have been advised against setting sail, and evacuation of people from vulnerable areas is underway, he said.
The armed forces have been put on alert, as have transport departments and medical teams.
